findings.summary: Logical assignment (`??=`, `||=`, `&&=`) stored a borrowed event without refusing, so the module-binding exemption's invariant (every store of an event into a module binding refuses) was false; both logical-assignment paths now compile their right side through the retained sink.

The invariant is enforced by one table test: 31 store forms into module bindings (plain, logical and destructuring assignment, element writes, array mutators, WeakSet/Map/Record/static-field stores, Object.assign, later-written closures, alias writes), each asserting the refusal at the store line.

An `EventTarget`-typed listener target resolves through one `domTargetIdentity(value) -> {target, engine}` extracted from `eventTargetCpp`, covering elements, Window, Document and the canvas instead of special-casing the two globals, with the engine following the value.
`refuseEscapingPlatformEventCapturesIn` and the closure classifier share one cached per-node read walk; `functionOfDeclaration` replaces three copies of the function-behind-a-declaration logic.
The transitive captured-symbol set is memoized per closure root and both caches are `BindingScopes` instance fields instead of a module-level map keyed only by node.

One `isReassignedFunctionLiteral` predicate and one `mayHoldBorrowedEvent(scope)` helper replace duplicated gates; `setInterval` keeps the stored function it was given instead of reading the variable at each tick, and timers accept stored functions with only optional or rest parameters.
Recursing into callback-record owners could switch shared calls to inline; generated neutrality over the registry shows no registered scene's C++ or WGSL moved.
